entities.name: Ashina Mishe
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ashina Mishe, a scion of the Western Turkic Khaganate's ruling Ashina clan, emerged as a pivotal figure in the mid-7th century CE, serving the expansionist Tang Dynasty as a general and ultimately as a Tang-appointed Khagan. Operating primarily across the vast plains and oases of Central Asia, his career (culminating in his death in 662 CE) underscores the complex interplay of nomadic power, imperial ambition, and strategic alliances that characterized the Classical era in East Asia. His significance lies in his instrumental role in integrating a substantial portion of the Western Turks into the Tang political and military orbit, thereby extending Chinese imperial influence deep into the Tarim Basin and beyond.

Mishe's rise is closely tied to the internal strife that plagued the Western Turkic Khaganate following the collapse of the Eastern Turkic Khaganate. After a period of initial resistance, he allied himself with the Tang, demonstrating unwavering loyalty to Emperor Taizong and later Emperor Gaozong. His most notable campaigns involved supporting Tang forces against rival Western Turkic factions, particularly those led by Ashina Helu, who sought to reassert independent Turkic supremacy. Mishe's military acumen and diplomatic skills proved invaluable in these conflicts, leading to his appointment by Emperor Gaozong in 657 CE as the "Shixing Khagan" (十姓可汗, Khagan of the Ten Tribes), effectively making him a Tang vassal ruler over a significant portion of the Western Turks, headquartered in the Dzungarian Basin.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ashina Mishe's strategic alliance and military service to the Tang Dynasty were instrumental in extending Chinese imperial control over significant portions of Central Asia, directly contributing to the subjugation of the Western Turkic Khaganate and the establishment of the Anxi Protectorate.
